scope: Independent read-only runtime/shared-wiring/UI source review and actual extracted controller/renderer tests with explicit synthetic owner/runtime seams.
findings: No remaining actionable source defect was found in the reviewed runtime/storage/schema, shared wiring or UI/action paths.

The identified textarea and pre first-LF display loss was corrected by one sacrificial opening newline at each element; actual rendered source checks pass. The original 15 modeled outcome objects remain unchanged within the final 16.
The final UI exposes an explicit password-and-consent recovery action. It forwards the original request and reviewed ledger digest and never resends.

source_traces.name: Dedicated/shared operation identity
source_traces.conclusion: Request graph and real ProviderGateway use twenty-i plus profile:revision:SHA256(credential ciphertext) and the same compact typed operation. Scope and audit contain content digests, never template source.

source_traces.name: Durable single attempt and replay
source_traces.conclusion: Owner-password admission atomically inserts the consumed grant and encrypted request; the shared ledger claims outside a transaction before the only non-idempotent attempt. Exact replay returns retained summary before DNS/key/send. Changed input refuses.

source_traces.name: Missing-terminal recovery
source_traces.conclusion: Only one-attempt, finished failed/uncertain/accepted_pending ledgers with exact fingerprint and unreconciled state can restore a missing terminal. Current owner/key and reviewed ledger digest are rechecked; recovery records attempted history and does not claim observation or delivery.

source_traces.name: Readback correspondence
source_traces.conclusion: Started reads precede effects; profile/time/state and owner context are validated before encrypted receipt storage. Verify requires eligible completion before the read and again before check insertion, compares exact decrypted bytes, and binds independent receipt/request/ledger hashes.

source_traces.name: Authority at effects
source_traces.conclusion: Raw client/contact/support provenance refuses. Current active owner auth and profile revision/credential ciphertext are rechecked around DNS, key opening, content resolution, transport and readback save. Grant revocation is checked at request authorization.

source_traces.name: Private authenticated storage
source_traces.conclusion: AES-GCM content uses installation/profile/event AAD; metadata HMAC, exact audit correspondence, count/head checkpoint and reverse grant/ledger correspondence authenticate history. Keyset batches retain ciphertext lengths only, and private open rereads and verifies one authenticated row.

source_traces.name: Preparation and history loss
source_traces.conclusion: Preparation requires existing provider-operation storage and original vault key. Marker/head/audit/table/grant/ledger inconsistencies refuse; empty pre-marker schema can be validated for explicit retry. No GET creates storage or opens provider transport.

source_traces.name: Admin dispatch and failed forms
source_traces.conclusion: POST-only outer action path checks CSRF then admin permission before the dedicated owner action. Failed final forms redisplay original ID/proof/base64 only after current proof equality; stale proof suppresses save. Source is escaped plain text.

source_traces.name: Narrow shared transport change
source_traces.conclusion: New supplier-dependent operation is unavailable to generic approval. Only exact reset-template POST receives the typed enlarged body bound. Other routes retain their 8192-byte bound and existing fixed-host/TLS/redirect/pinning policies.

limits: No SQL, installed application HTTP, provider call, provider email delivery, or live mutation was executed.
The 16 checks per PHP mode execute actual controller/renderer bodies but stub owner/runtime services. The outer CSRF rejection is modeled; actual action-source ordering was separately inspected.
The first-LF textarea rule is modeled, not a browser engine test. Browser normal CR/LF form normalization happens before review; exact final base64 confirmation preserves the reviewed bytes.
Existing foundation and offline regression reports are referenced as retained runs, not executed again for this review.
